system:
You are the hardware architect in a design-space exploration loop for a
CORDIC sin/cos unit as an ASIC in the open sky130 standard-cell library
(sky130_fd_sc_hd, typical corner).

Division of labour (strict):
- YOU choose architecture families and parameter ranges from the registry below,
  read compact summaries of results, and decide what to do next.
- CODE does all the numbers: a bit-accurate model gives exact accuracy, an
  analytical cost model gives cell-area/FF/Fmax estimates, Optuna NSGA-II searches inside
  the ranges you choose, and Pareto/hypervolume maths ranks the results.
- Never estimate, predict or invent area, gate counts, FFs, Fmax, throughput, power or error
  figures. Reason only from the numbers in the summaries you are given.

Architecture registry (the only families and parameters that exist):
- `iterative`: 1 micro-rotation/cycle, shared datapath with barrel shifters; N+3 cycles/result
    - `data_width` (8..28): angle input and sin/cos output width W (Q1.(W-2) output)
    - `n_iter` (4..30): number of micro-rotations N
    - `angle_guard` (-2..4): angle path / atan-LUT width minus W (A = W + angle_guard)
    - `frac_guard` (0..4): extra fractional bits on x and y
    - `rounding` (trunc|round): shift and output rounding
- `unrolled_k`: k chained micro-rotations/cycle, shared FSM; ceil(N/k)+3 cycles/result
    - `data_width` (8..28): angle input and sin/cos output width W (Q1.(W-2) output)
    - `n_iter` (4..30): number of micro-rotations N
    - `angle_guard` (-2..4): angle path / atan-LUT width minus W (A = W + angle_guard)
    - `frac_guard` (0..4): extra fractional bits on x and y
    - `rounding` (trunc|round): shift and output rounding
    - `k` (2..8): micro-rotations per cycle
- `pipelined`: one registered stage per micro-rotation; 1 result/cycle, N+2 latency
    - `data_width` (8..28): angle input and sin/cos output width W (Q1.(W-2) output)
    - `n_iter` (4..30): number of micro-rotations N
    - `angle_guard` (-2..4): angle path / atan-LUT width minus W (A = W + angle_guard)
    - `frac_guard` (0..4): extra fractional bits on x and y
    - `rounding` (trunc|round): shift and output rounding
- `pipelined_m`: register every m stages; 1 result/cycle, ceil(N/m)+2 latency
    - `data_width` (8..28): angle input and sin/cos output width W (Q1.(W-2) output)
    - `n_iter` (4..30): number of micro-rotations N
    - `angle_guard` (-2..4): angle path / atan-LUT width minus W (A = W + angle_guard)
    - `frac_guard` (0..4): extra fractional bits on x and y
    - `rounding` (trunc|round): shift and output rounding
    - `m` (2..8): micro-rotations between pipeline registers

Goal: map the feasible Pareto front over the spec's objectives as well as possible
within the evaluation budget (scored by hypervolume against the spec's reference
point); the final design is then picked from that front by the spec's selection
rule. Both matter: the hypervolume rewards covering the whole trade-off curve, not
just the corner the selection rule picks. Before the run ends, code spends a reserved
part of the budget mapping the front over the full ranges of the families you found on
it. If no design in the registry can meet the constraints, say so (decision
`infeasible`) rather than settling for a design that violates them.

Notes:
- Accuracy depends only on data_width, n_iter, angle_guard, frac_guard and rounding
  (all families compute identical bits); output LSB is 2^-(data_width-2).
- iterative/unrolled_k produce one result every several cycles; pipelined/pipelined_m
  produce one result per cycle.
- Ranges are inclusive. Narrow ranges focus the evaluation budget; ranges outside the
  registry are clamped by code.

Metrics:
- ffs: estimated flip-flops
- fmax_mhz: estimated max clock (MHz)
- throughput_msps: estimated results per microsecond = Fmax x results/cycle
- latency_cycles: cycles from input to output (exact, from the schedule)
- latency_ns: latency in ns at Fmax (estimate)
- power_index: relative power index, reference iterative @100 MHz = 1.0 (estimate, not watts)
- max_abs_err: max |error| vs ideal sin/cos, absolute (exact)
- rms_err: RMS error, absolute (exact)
- accuracy_bits: -log2(max_abs_err) (exact)
- area_um2: ASIC: estimated standard-cell area in um^2 (sky130_fd_sc_hd)
- gate_eq: ASIC: estimated area in NAND2 gate equivalents (area / 3.7536 um^2)

families.why: Area is the only objective and the 1 MSPS constraint is trivially met by a shared datapath (N+3 cycles at a few hundred MHz is still several MSPS), so the area-minimal family should own the front; the box spans the accuracy threshold (W>=12, N>=12) up to comfortably-above-2^-10 designs so the area/accuracy trade-off curve is covered.

Replicates the datapath k-fold for throughput we do not need, so it should be area-dominated, but a small share checks whether any k gives a cheaper register/shifter mix at the same accuracy and keeps the front honest.

Large m approaches the iterative area while still giving 1 result/cycle; worth probing in case its higher Fmax lets a smaller W/N meet the error bound at lower area, and it is the most plausible non-iterative front member.
One full-width register per micro-rotation makes this the most area-expensive family; a small share confirms it is dominated and guards against an unexpected Fmax/area interaction.

parsed.rationale: The spec's only objective is cell area with a loose 1 MSPS throughput floor and a 2^-10 error ceiling, so the front should be dominated by the smallest-area family (iterative) at accuracies just above the threshold, with larger W/N buying accuracy at higher area. I give iterative the majority of round-1 budget over a box that brackets the accuracy threshold (W 10-22, N 8-26, both guard ranges, both rounding modes, since round can buy accuracy for free area-wise) and spend the remainder on the three parallel families at narrower boxes to verify they are dominated and to catch any surprise front member. Later rounds will re-allocate toward whichever family actually holds the front and toward the accuracy/area knee.

  ranges of the families on the front, seeded with it); use it when the front covers

parsed.rationale: All 10 Pareto points are `iterative`; the other families are strictly worse on the area axis (best feasible area: iterative 7806 um^2, unrolled_k 9607, pipelined_m 24396, pipelined 47147). Under a min-area objective with only a >=1 MSPS / <=2^-10 error constraint, the feasible throughput is met everywhere (best seen 201 MSPS) and the error constraint is met by the whole front (worst front point 2^-11.78), so both the min-area pick and the hypervolume live in the iterative family. The front is nevertheless only a thin slice of the trade-off: data_width spans 16..20 of the registry's 8..28, and accuracy_bits spans 11.8..16.6 against an HV accuracy reference of 10, so the staircase's top end is truncated at 16.6 bits while nothing below area 7806 was found feasible. Both the low-area end (smaller data_width with enough n_iter/guard bits, error floor of ~2^-(W-1) still leaves headroom to the 2^-10 limit) and the high-accuracy end (larger data_width/n_iter) are unexplored, and each end carries large HV weight because the area reference is 40000. A full-range NSGA-II over the on-front family, seeded with the current front, is therefore the highest-value use of this round; refinement around the current narrow band would only re-sample the same region.

parsed.rationale: Spend the final 100-eval round mapping the front over the full ranges of the families on it. The spec selection rule is min area_um2, and every Pareto design is `iterative` (best feasible areas elsewhere are unrolled_k 9607, pipelined_m 24396, pipelined 47147, so the other families cannot win the area objective and need no further refinement). The front currently spans accuracy_bits 11.8..23.9, but the binding accuracy constraint is only 2^-10 (~10 bits) and the front's lowest-accuracy point is 11.8 bits — the mandatory region between 10 and 11.8 bits is entirely unmapped, and the feasible data_width range on the front (15..28, registry min 8) shows smaller/less-accurate designs than the current best (iterative dw=16 N=23, area 7806, 11.8 bits) are reachable, which is exactly how the area axis gets pushed below 7806 and the HV reference plane at area 40000 is better covered. The right end also has headroom (max accuracy seen 23.89 bits vs registry data_width up to 28). With HV still improving (+8.9% last round) and the front covering only part of the area/accuracy range, a seeded NSGA-II sweep over the full iterative (and, for completeness, the other feasible on-front) ranges is the highest-value use of the reserved budget.
